result.stopReason: Relaxing checkP alone is unsound, and closing the hole is a second design decision, which is the stop CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:85 names for this rung. checkP is not an accident of the checker. It is the Fortress designers' own rule, "multiple instantiation exclusion": the OOPSLA 2011 paper adopts it by name (Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152), and Naden's 2012-08-31 writeup says "Fortress implements blanket multiple instantiation exclusion" (Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497). The compiled checker's Return Type Rule check solves for a single instantiation of the generic, which is sound only while that rule holds (OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105). A six-line BadList program shows the hole: probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss has object Both extends {Tag[String], Tag[ZZ32]}, a generic pick[X] beside a pick specialised for Tag[ZZ32], and y: Tag[String] = pick(Both). With the relaxation it type-checks under all three placements (hierarchy only, hierarchy plus overloading, broad) and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError: IntTag does not implement Tag[String] (probe-matrix.txt:67, :89, :111). The base checker refuses the program. Making the compiled path sound again needs one of two choices, and both are Pavol's. Either keep the rule on the compiled path, and then the interpreter library's nested tower cannot be checked as it stands. Or drop the rule together with enforcing Specification/basic/overloading.tex:100-105 (declarations whose static parameters differ are an error), which is decision (b) of perf-probes/nat/triage.md:52-59, :113, already reserved to him.

Rung P stopped and lands no checker change. The clause it was to relax, checkP, is the Fortress designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion" (OOPSLA 2011, Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152; Naden 2012, justificationOfRTR.tex:476-478, :496-497). The compiled checker enforces it in the two hierarchy questions and relies on it in the Return Type Rule check (OverloadingOracle.scala:81-105). The trace, the triage and the batch record never cite it. The batch record's "designers' survey" is a revival-era note (run-c4/.../D/SURVEY.md:46).
All measurements used one build with an instance-held switch (probes/measurement-switch.patch); the source tree is back at the base.
Under every placement (hierarchy only, hierarchy plus overloading, broad) a six-line BadList program type-checks and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError: a variable typed Tag[String] holds an object that is only a Tag[ZZ32]. The base checker refuses the program.
The interpreter took the other side of the trade-off. It has no instantiation clause, and it refuses generic overloads that have no excluding pair. The specification sides with the interpreter on both halves (types-vals-vars.tex:184-189; overloading.tex:100-105). Rung P as briefed is the one unsound combination: the interpreter's half on inheritance with the compiler's half on overloading.

result.forPavol:
THE FORK. The compiled checker's checkP is the 2011-2012 team's "multiple instantiation exclusion" (Papers/Types/exclusion.tick:141-152; justificationOfRTR.tex:496-497). The specification refuses it (types-vals-vars.tex:184-189; trait-parameters.tex:359-367 and :383-397, whose object Empty belongs to every instantiation of List) and the library route needs it gone (61 of the 93 errors, CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:73). Removing it in any placement opens one hole: the compiled overloading checker's Return Type Rule trusts the single instantiation the rule used to guarantee (OverloadingOracle.scala:88-95), and a six-line program then type-checks and dies with IncompatibleClassChangeError (probes/ProbeMIEPick.fss; probe-matrix.txt:67, :89, :111). Which rule replaces that reliance is yours, because the natural one is the sentence already reserved to you as triage decision (b).

CANDIDATES AND COSTS. (a) The specification's sentence, overloading.tex:100-108: overloads of a name share their static parameters, one instantiation per call site. Closes the hole; the checker's side of the instantiation question goes away. Cost: refuses generic-beside-non-generic sets that have no hole — compiler_tests/Compiled12.invariantInference.fss:52-61 (gated by its .test), Compiled6.ak.fss:14-15, Library/Generator2.fss:52-57, four interpreter tests (overloadTest8, doubledOverloading, GeneratorNullPointer, ArrayListQuick/PureListQuick) — so gated tests would be rewritten, itself a reserved stop (PLAN.md:52); the triage's 35 library sites, already errors, then need renames not a checker accommodation; and "static parameters" for functional methods of generic traits must be defined (triage.md:57-59) or the sentence refuses overrides. (b) The hole's exact shape as a sub-rule of the sentence: refuse a pair where one declaration has static parameters the other lacks and the generic one's return type depends on such a parameter, unless the more specific return type is a subtype with the parameter held rigid. Closes the hole, refuses nothing the specification permits, accepts every corpus site above, leaves decision (b) untouched; one edit in OverloadingOracle.satisfiesReturnTypeRule. Cost: sound only if the code generator dispatches generic overloads at the call site's instantiation — unmeasured; a probe (generic-beside-generic with different bounds, on a multiply-instantiated object, static type one instantiation) settles it, and if dispatch is by inspection the rule must widen to generic-beside-generic pairs, which is then against the specification in that corner. (c) The interpreter's rule (OverloadedFunction.java:496-498), under which the library was written: against the specification for same-parameter generic overloads with unrelated overlapping domains; compiled cost unmeasured. (d) Keep the rule: against the specification and the library route; not recommended.

RECOMMENDATION. (b), landed in one rung together with the relaxation (hierarchy questions plus the overloading check, as the record placed it), preceded by the codegen measurement; the full sentence stays your separate decision (b) on the library evidence and subsumes it if taken. result.refusalReason: The new default overwrites a rendering that already worked. The compiled asString of an RR32 value and of a StringVector must answer what it answered on the base tree. Today `x: RR32 = 1.5; println(x)` prints `RR32` where the base printed `1.5` (walk also prints `1.5`), and a StringVector prints `StringVector` where it printed `[a b ]`. The cause: FRR32 and FStringVector are the 2 of the 17 value classes in compiler/runtimeValues/ whose Fortress trait declares no asString (CompilerBuiltin.fss:988-990, :1150-1155) and whose Java class declares no asString() (FStringVector.java:34 misspells it `asSring`). The old default jAsString(self) therefore reached their own Java toString (FRR32.java:19, FStringVector.java:24). The new jTypeName(self) returns the type name instead. Repair it so that a class with a Java toString of its own keeps it, for example with one or two lines in the native.
